title: Austin's 1895 Cotton Mill & Water System
summary:
• **Major investment opportunity**: City Council debated a major proposition from George N. Todd to build a large cotton factory in Austin. The project promised significant growth, including construction within 18 months with 15,000 spindles initially and expansion to 30,000 spindles over five years. The city would provide free water/power for 25 years.

• **Water and electric systems launching**: The city's new water and electric light systems were operational, with over 500 water customers and 106 electric light applications already filed. The council approved contracts to supply water and electricity to the Deaf and Dumb Asylum and the International & Great Northern Railroad.

• **Debt management and financial restructuring**: The council approved a complex series of bond exchanges designed to reduce the city's $1.4 million waterworks debt by $50,000, with the Finance Committee recommending strategic purchases of lower-cost bonds.

• **Infrastructure and safety regulations**: The council passed fire safety ordinance requirements for escape routes at public gathering places and authorized citizens to privately construct water line extensions at their own expense, expanding service to underserved areas.

• **Public services expansion**: Monthly reports showed the city providing hospitalization, cemetery services, fire protection, and police services. Officers also managed water distribution challenges as demand grew faster than infrastructure could reach outlying areas.

G. N. Todd's Proposition to estab-
-lish Cotton Factory. &c.
First. G. N. Todd to purchase a tract of land 25 to 50 acres in 90 days inside or just
outside city limits.
Second. To build thereon within 18 months a factory building and equip same with 15000
spindles, 350 looms and other machinery and increase same from time to time during five
years to 30000 spindles and 700 looms and other machinery.
Third. To permit citizens of Austin to obtain a co-operative interest in said plant of
$25000, payable in 12 monthly payments to one of the Austin banks to be paid by said bank
to the mills company upon the following conditions and terms: Ten per cent upon purchase
of said land and commencing work on the factory; 20 per cent when factory is half
completed; 20 per cent upon completion of factory and the remainder 50 per cent upon
installment of 15000 spindles and 350 looms in said factory.
The said $25000 to be preferred stock and entitled to 10 per cent dividends before stock
and its prorata share of common stock dividends.
Thus giving the citizens a share of the profits of the enterprise and making it a
community interest, affording protection to the mills.
In consideration of the fulfillment of these agreements the city is to furnish said plant
sufficient water or electric power to operate all its machinery not to exceed 1000 horse
power free of charge for 25 years and at a fixed charge thereafter to be agreed upon not
to exceed $50 per annum for each horse power used. A failure of said Todd or said mills
company to fulfill any of its agreement herein stated to forfeit its franchise.
Fourth. Todd to furnish city $2500 upon completion of building in 8 months, the mills to
be located at the dam or anywhere in city limits or just outside.
Proposition referred.
Alderman Taylor moved that the proposition and petition be referred to a special committee
of five to confer with a committee from the Board of Trade concerning same. The motion
prevailed and the chair appointed Aldermen Taylor Quinn, Tobin, Townsend and Nitschke as
the committee on the part of the council.

Report on petition of Y.M.C.A.
Alderman Taylor, for the committee on ordinances, to whom was referred the petition of the
Board of Directors of the Young Men's Christian Association and others asking for the
repeal of an ordinance entitled "An ordinance providing for the protection of persons
attending theaters and other public places of amusements and fixing a penalty for the
violation hereof", presented a report thereon which states that they "have given the
matter mature consideration and investigation and we are unable to concur in the opinion
expressed by petitioners that its enforcement will cause great hardship and serious
injury. It will hardly be contended that the enforcement of an ordinance, having for its
purpose the protection of life and limb, will work a great hardship and serious injury to
persons owning or leasing buildings, room or part of a room wherein any hall or other
public amusement is given or held, nor do we believe it will be contended that places of
worship, such as the First Baptist church, the Tenth street Methodist church and the
Christian church can be properly termed 'places of public amusement' within the meaning of
the ordinance. Your committee finds that a building affected by the provisions of the
ordinance, having a number of windows, may be furnished with the necessary fire escapes at
a trifling cost, compared with the loss of life and injury that might result in case of
fire with no means of escape. In case of the Board of Trade building, the opera house and
the Young Men's Christian Association hall, two or more fire escapes, to the ground,
properly connected with all the windows by an iron balcony, would conform to the
requirements of the ordinance. We therefore return the petition with the recommendation
that it be not granted and further, that section 3 be so amended as to hereafter read as
follows: "Section 3. That any person or persons violating any of the provisions of
sections 1, 2, and 5A of this ordinance shall on conviction, be fined not less than
twenty-five dollars nor more than one hundred dollars." Aldermen Lumbers moved that the
petition be referred back to the committee on ordinances and that the city engineer be
instructed to confer with owners or persons in charge of buildings affected by the
ordinance and report the result of such conference to said committee to

The ordinance provides that citizens of Austin may lay water mains, under the supervision
of the superintendent of the water and light system, for the purpose of connecting their
premises with the city’s water mains and that the actual cost of all pipe laid under the
provisions of the ordinance shall be filed with the superintendent of water and light
system as soon as such work is completed. Provided that the cost of labor and pipe shall
be approved by the water and light commission, and no connection shall be allowed unless
the cost of the same shall not exceed the amount which it would cost the city to do the
work, and the city shall have the right at any time to purchase all pipe laid at its
actual cost, from which shall be deducted any and all sums paid by citizens who have paid
the owners for the privilege of connecting therewith.
All persons who avail themselves of the privilege of laying pipes or connecting therewith,
shall pay to the city the regular prices charged by it to water takers.
